kernel: bottom_scan<T,vecT,256> (src/cuda/level1/scan/scan_kernel.h), launched by the driver for <float,float4> and <double,double4> as <<<64,256,2*sizeof(T)*256>>>

sites.source: val_4.x += res + s_seed;  val_4.y += res + s_seed;  val_4.z += res + s_seed;  val_4.w += res + s_seed;
sites.operation: ld.shared (SASS: LDS R8, [RZ] at 0x06b0 in the first unrolled window copy, attributed to L298 (the four uses of s_seed are one load); further copies at 0x0bc0, 0x0fe0; s_seed is the static __shared__ T at shared offset 0, the dynamic sdata starts at 0x10). Executed by all 256 threads of the block.
st.shared (SASS: @!P0 STS [RZ], R7 at 0x0740 in the first window copy; further copies 0x0c90 (@!P2), 0x10a0 (@!P2)). Executed only by thread blockSize-1 = 255 (warp 7).

thread_pair_example: bottom_scan<float,float4,256>, grid 64 x block 256, size 262144 -> region 1024 vec4 per block = 4 windows of 256 vec4 (windows 0..3), block b, any window w: thread 5 (warp 0) reads s_seed at L298-L301 after the last barrier inside scanLocalMem (L185), while thread 255 (warp 7) writes s_seed = val_4.w at L309; nothing orders them, so if warp 7 gets there first thread 5 (and any other lagging thread) adds the NEXT window's seed (WAR). Same code for <double,double4,256>.
class_reason: Two pairs, two classes (record: DR+SC). (1) s_seed is a plain __shared__ T: both the read (L298-L301) and the write (L309) are ordinary LDS/STS, no volatile, no atomic, so the unordered cross-warp WAR is a data race (DR). (2) the extra pair on the dynamic shared array sdata (extra_pairs) goes through 'volatile T* s_data' in scanLocalMem, so both accesses are volatile (strong): the unordered conflict is SC. verify.expected_report_buggy: 'DR for the s_seed pair (cross-warp); SC for the sdata cross-window pair (volatile vs volatile)'.
buggy_expected: Two findings in bottom_scan: (1) DR, shared WAR on s_seed (read L298-L301 vs write L309, cross-warp); (2) SC, shared sdata, volatile read L198 in window w vs volatile writes L147/L152 of window w+1 (extra_pairs).

fixed.reason: The fix adds __syncthreads() after the initial s_seed load (fixed L274; redundant, scanLocalMem's barriers already order the init) and, the important one, __syncthreads() immediately before the s_seed update inside the window loop (fixed L311, SASS BAR.SYNC at 0x0760 / 0x0cb0 / 0x10b0, between the s_seed read LDS 0x06c0 and the update STS 0x0770). That barrier orders all reads of s_seed (L301-L304 in the fixed file) and all volatile sdata reads of scanLocalMem (L198) in window w before the writes of s_seed and the next window's sdata writes (L147/L152). Nothing is expected for either pair (verify.expected_report_fixed). The barriers are at loop-body level in a loop whose trip count is uniform per block (while (window < block_stop)), so every thread of the block reaches them.

sites.operation: ld.volatile.shared (SASS LDS R15, [R0.X4+0x40c] at 0x06c0 in the first window copy; 0x0bd0, 0x0ff0 in the others)

sites.source: s_data[idx] = val;   (idx = threadIdx.x + blockSize; L147 'idx = threadIdx.x; s_data[idx] = 0.0f;' is the second write that can hit the same cell: thread 255 clears s_data[255] which thread 0 returns from at L198)
sites.operation: st.volatile.shared (SASS STS [R0.X4+0x410], R11 at 0x0850 / 0x0cc0 in the window copies after the first; L147 is STS [R0.X4+0x10], RZ at 0x0810 / 0x0ca0)

extra_pairs.thread_relation: cross-warp-same-block (thread 0 / warp 0 reads s_data[255] at L198 vs thread 255 / warp 7 clears it at L147 in the next window) and intra-warp (the record's example: thread 17 reads s_data[272] at L198 vs thread 16 writes s_data[272] at L152 in the next window; both in warp 0)
extra_pairs.note: scanLocalMem is called once per window; its first writes (L147, L152) of window w+1 follow the L198 read of window w with only the s_seed code in between and, in the buggy file, no barrier. In the fixed file the barrier L311 sits between them.

sass_notes: sm_89, nvdisasm -g of the driver built with -lineinfo (the lineinfo check of the R2 route is SAME: targets/lit-arrayfire-1/lineinfo.check). bottom_scan<float,float4,256> (and the double instance) are emitted with the window loop unrolled into several copies (three copies of the L298 / L309 pair in the float kernel: 0x06b0/0x0740, 0x0bc0/0x0c90, 0x0fe0/0x10a0), so detectors may report several SASS addresses for the same source line. Inside scanLocalMem every step has BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING (L153, L157, L158, ...; last at L185, 0x06a0 in the first copy); between that last barrier and the STS at L309 (0x0740) there is no BAR. Fixed: BAR.SYNC at L274 (0x0250), and at L311 (0x0760, 0x0cb0, 0x10b0) directly before the @!P STS [RZ] of L313. All shared accesses, volatile or not, are plain LDS / STS on sm_89 (no .STRONG token on any site, no WARPSYNC emitted in these kernels), so the volatile qualifier of the sdata pair is not visible as a SASS token. The other kernels of the header (reduce, scan_single_block) are compiled and launched by the driver in both variants.
derived_from: verify.accesses + verify.thread_pair of targets.jsonl, re-checked against src/cuda/level1/scan/scan_kernel.h@785d9ee (and @700ab82 for the fixed lines: L274, L311, L313; the commit also reformats lines) on 2026-10-20; lines and SASS offsets taken from the file as compiled (R2 harness file name = repo path).
open_questions: The same header also contains the reduce kernel (L126-L131), a warp-synchronous tail reduction on volatile shared memory (sdata[tid] += sdata[tid + 32] ... + 1 for tid < warpSize) with no __syncwarp. It is identical in the buggy and the fixed file, is not part of the registered pair and may be reported by a detector in both variants as an intra-warp finding unrelated to the fix; the oracle does not register it.

Native manifestation (sm_75 smoke build on c38, not a deliverable): the buggy float run FAILS the host check in every run (10 runs: 128, 256, 512, 640, 768 or 896 mismatching elements of 262144), the double run passed, and the fixed variant passes both in all 10 runs. This is the s_seed race becoming visible; the sm_89 native phase will show whether it also appears there.

review.notes: R2 harness: every copied kernel file under r2/buggy and r2/fixed is byte-identical (cmp) to git show <buggy_commit>:<path> / <fix_commit>:<path>; git diff buggy..fix of those files is exactly the fix hunk described in fixed.reason. (the fix commit also strips trailing whitespace, so most changed lines are whitespace only). Primary pair confirmed at 785d9ee: s_seed is a plain '__shared__ T s_seed' (scan_kernel.h:251); all threads read it at L298-301 after scanLocalMem's last barrier (L185 for blockSize 256), thread blockSize-1 = 255 writes it at L309, no barrier in between (scan_kernel.h:185-309) -> plain/plain cross-warp WAR, DR. Geometry: float: n/4 = 65536 vec4, region 1024 per block, 4 windows; double: 2 windows (driver.cu:19,41). extra_pairs confirmed: the L198 read s_data[idx-1] (idx = tid + 256) of window w and the L147 / L152 writes of window w+1 have no barrier between them; both cross-warp (thread 0 reads s_data[255], thread 255 clears it at L147; thread 32k reads s_data[32k+255], thread 32k-1 writes it at L152) and intra-warp instances exist. The accesses go through 'volatile T* s_data' (scan_kernel.h:143,248,295). Fixed (700ab82): __syncthreads() at L274 and at L311 inside the window loop (trip count uniform per block: window, block_start, block_stop depend on blockIdx only), ordering both the s_seed reads (L301-304) and the L198 sdata reads before the L313 write and the next window's L147/L152 writes. 'absent' confirmed for both pairs; the reduce kernel's warp-synchronous volatile tail (L126-131, unchanged) remains in both variants, as open_questions[0] says. depends_on_D20 = true: the SC half of 'DR+SC' is the sdata pair, which is volatile *shared* memory. At PTX level (ld/st.volatile.shared) it is a strong/strong conflict, SC. The oracle's own sass_notes say these accesses are plain LDS/STS on sm_89 with no .STRONG token (not re-verified here); under the token rule (D9) a SASS-based detector would then class that pair DR, and the target would be DR only. Which reading counts is the D20 decision (together with whether shared-memory volatile counts as strong as compiled); expected_class left as 'DR+SC'. The s_seed pair is DR under either reading. Not independently verified: the SASS opcodes, register operands and offsets quoted in sites/sass_notes (the one permitted srun on -p normal could not start: partition fully allocated, estimated start 2026-10-21 14:37, so the job was cancelled); access widths were checked from the source types instead. Native-run and smoke-run statements in open_questions are builder results and were not reviewed.
